relevance_note: The cohort includes five individually described HA20 patients with TNFAIP3 variants: 'Five patients (cases 5, 10, 14, 29, 31) were classified as having Haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20)'.
method_note: Worked by reading the whole paper (main text, Table 1, supplementary PDF text) and building the JSON with a short Python script whose values and spans I typed from my reading; a check confirmed every span occurs verbatim. Table 1 has patients as rows; spans quote the row from the case label through the cell where under ~300 characters, otherwise the unique cell text (e.g. Case 29's long rows, treatment/outcome cells). Some supplementary spans contain the PDF line breaks verbatim. Scope: only the five HA20 cases (5, 10, 14, 29, 31) and relatives described in relation to them; the other 26 cohort members (other genes or no variant) get no rows (cohort of 31). Maternal cousins of Case 29 ('maternal cousins had similar but milder symptoms') were not given rows because their number is not stated. Labels use 'Case N' (the paper's 'case N' form). Ages in Table 1 are 'Age at the time of this study' (note b), recorded as age at last evaluation; years taken from the cohort description. is_proband left null for the cases (pedigree arrows in Supplementary Fig. S2 are not available as text). Vital status not stated explicitly, left 'not reported'. Variant class not stated in words for any TNFAIP3 variant ('not reported'); inheritance left 'not reported' for Case 29 although the mother carries the variant (not stated as inherited). Transcript not printed (note d cites an HGNC RefSeq transcript without an ID). Table 1 prints cDNA without 'c.'; recorded as printed, including the space in '1625_1626insGAC TACAGCAGAGGCC'. In-silico predictions (SIFT/PolyPhen2/MutationTaster) not recorded as functional evidence. Contradictions/inconsistencies: (1) Table 1 lists two TNFAIP3 variants for Case 10 (946G>A G316S and the S548Dfs*128 insertion), but the text names only p.S548Dfs*128 as Case 10's HA20 variant; both are recorded. (2) Table 1 gives variant classification 3 (unknown significance) for all TNFAIP3 variants, whereas the Discussion says six of the seven novel proposed disease-causing variants (all but p.T76I) can be classified as pathogenic per ACMG; both recorded in pathogenicity. (3) Main text says the NF-κB assay showed upregulation 'in all four cases'; Supplementary Fig. S1 says Case 29 showed less activation (attributed to treatment). (4) Case 14: Table 1 says 'chronic pulmonary interstitial emphysema', the text says 'chronic interstitial pneumonia'; both emitted as observed features. (5) Case 31: perianal ulceration 'first noticed at 2 weeks of age, followed by recurrent fevers from birth'. 'Mother, but not other mildly affected relatives, also found to have' the Case 29 variant is ambiguous on whether the other relatives were tested negative or untested; no variant rows given to them. Checklist judgements: Case 5 'redness of the eyes' not counted as ocular inflammation; headaches not counted as CNS involvement; Case 29 livedo reticularis counted as a skin lesion; Case 31 perianal ulcers/abscess/fistula not counted as gastrointestinal inflammation and recurrent tonsilitis not counted as recurrent infections; autoimmune hypothyroidism counted as autoimmune thyroiditis; chronic interstitial pneumonia counted as interstitial lung disease. 'Similar features/symptoms' of relatives recorded as one vague observed feature each, with all checklist items 'not reported'.
